Guidance & outlook: Auto ROCE continued to be strong at 68% on a trailing twelve -month basis, against 72% for FY26.
This is the walk from PBT before exceptional items of ₹1,635 crore in Q1 FY26 to ₹2,057 crore in Q1 FY27, and what you see below is the EBIT margin bridge.
Coming to Free cash flow - for the quarter, FCF was ₹1,114 crore, against negative of ₹1,796 crore in Q1 FY26 - a swing of about ₹2,900 crore.
Growth & demand: The volume momentum we saw in the last page translated into a 23% revenue growth for the quarter, which stood at ₹19,300 crore, EBITDA was ₹2,300 crore at a margin of 11.7%, down 60 basis points YoY .
We also had 110 bps growth in VAHAN share in small commercial vehicle and around 490 bps growth in CV passenger, which is buses and vans.

Moving onto our businesses, starting with trucks, we have a YoY market share gain due to volume growth, especially in heavy commercial vehicles on the back of the new product launches that we spoke earlier.
Margins & costs: EBIT margin was 9.4%, down only 20 basis points and PBT before exceptional items was ₹2,100 crore, up 26% year-on-year.
The price increases that we took during the quarter have largely been passed through and together these added 140 basis points to EBIT margin.
Net of all this, EBIT margin moved from 9.6% to 9.4%. and in summary, operating leverage and improved realisation have absorbed almost all of the significant commodity headwind.
Capex & expansion: We also crossed a major milestone, with our Lucknow plant crossing 10 lakh commercial vehicles in cumulative production.
On Freight Tiger - we acquired an additional 18.1% equity stake in May 2026 for around ₹96 crore, taking our total holding to approximately 63.6%.
In terms of capacity of Intra EV, our in-house capacity is not a challenge at all.
Balance sheet & cash: Free cash flow was ₹1,100 crore, against a negative ₹1,800 crore in Q1 last year.
Net cash stood at ₹7,100 crore as of June 30th, against ₹7,500 crore at March-end and this is after the ₹1,473 crore dividend payout during the quarter.
Consolidated free cash flow was ₹400 crore against a negative of ₹2,000 crore in Q1 of FY26.
Risks & challenges: Variable costs were the principal headwind at ₹649 crore, or 340 basis points.
Steel, aluminium and copper flowing through into material cost, consistent with the headwinds that we flagged when we closed FY26.
ILMCV saw a slight drop essentially due to the supply chain challenges that we have seen, especially in the Western Zone.

Guidance & outlook: While I'm really pleased with the margin story, EBITDA margins have expanded from 7.8% in FY23 to 13.2% in FY26.
International business continues its growth trajectory with YoY growth at 17% in Q4 and 54% for the full year FY26, mainly led by the SAARC countries.
So, we expect FY27 also our guidance would remain similar, 2% to 4% of revenue .
Growth & demand: As far as volume is concerned, the offtake TIV grew 19% YoY in Q4 while Tata Motors volumes outpaced the industry at 25% YoY growth.
For FY26, the TIV growth was 12.5%, and it marked the highest ever annual volume, whereas Tata Motors grew 11.6% YoY.
E -way bill generation grew 15% on a YoY basis in Q4 and, in fact, accelerated to 19% YoY growth in March 2026.
Margins & costs: EBITDA margin expanded steadily through the year and exited Q4 at 13.9%, up 130 bps YoY.
Higher volume , mix, price realisation together contributed nearly 250 basis points to EBIT margin improvement.
Variable cost impact of 50 bps on account of elevated material cost due to inflation in key commodities, including steel, aluminium, and copper.
Capex & expansion: Reflecting our focus on operational excellence, Pantnagar plant received the Golden Peacock Award for Quality, and we also won multiple honors at the Apollo CV Awards 2026.
Overall, despite commodity headwinds, business delivered another quarter of strong structural margin expansion driven by higher volume, better mix, and improved realization .
I think for the last couple of years we've been giving guidance on CapEx of 2% to 4% of revenue, and we've been very consistent in meeting that.
Balance sheet & cash: With disciplined working capital management for the full year , free cash flow was R s.
Moving on to the cash flow now, as mentioned earlier, our free cash flow is growing consistently over the years.
Working capital remained very well controlled with trade receivables at Rs.
Risks & challenges: The freight index edged up quarter -on-quarter through Q4 on the back of firm consumption which softened a bit in March and April.
On the supply side, we did see for international business vessel transit delays, which were then proactively managed and exposure to affected trans -shipment hubs like Dubai/Doha has been contained.
We are cautiously looking at near-term headwinds, especially the commodity headwinds, which I already see a few questions being asked about and a subdued sentiment in Middle East and North Africa.

Guidance & outlook: FY27 Key Priorities The commercial vehicle industry is expected to sustain its growth trajectory in FY27, albeit at a more moderate pace, reflecting a strong base from FY26 and near-term headwinds including commodity cost pressure, geopolitical uncertainty and potential demand implications of new regulatory requirements.
The Union Budget for FY27 has proposed a capital expenditure outlay of H12.22 lakh crore, up from H11.21 lakh crore in FY26.
Outlook Looking ahead, the IMF expects GDP growth of 6.5% in FY27, reaffirming confidence in India's long-term structural growth drivers.
Growth & demand: During the year, your Company further consolidated this leadership, driven by focused product interventions, disciplined sales execution and deeper, more meaningful customer engagement, delivering sales volumes of over 4,35,000 vehicles, compared to ~3,85,000 vehicles in the previous year-representing a robust year on year growth of 13%.
Additionally, we had a notable resurgence in our Heavy Commercial Vehicle (HCV) Segment, which achieved its highest market share to 55% in a decade.
Performance Anchored in Execution Discipline Against this backdrop, Tata Motors Commercial Vehicles delivered 14% (excluding TDM) volume growth in FY26.
Margins & costs: Profitability strengthened further, with EBITDA margins of 12.3%, reflecting improved operating leverage and disciplined cost management.

With more than 30% of beneficiaries from marginalized communities, these efforts reaffirm our commitment to inclusive and sustainable development, spanning key focus areas such as water conservation, education, skill development and healthcare.
Given the highly competitive nature of the commercial vehicle industry, the ability to pass through input cost inflation through price increases remains constrained.
